name: Holy Roman Empire

areaKm2.note: Wikipedia infobox gives 1.1 million km2 (c. 1150, high), including imperial Italy and Burgundy. The world_1200 union (Holy Roman Empire + Burgandy) measures 0.69 million km2 on the sphere (low); it under-draws imperial Italy. Mid is a compromise.

population.note: HYDE/Gapminder country series for 1200 (OWID): Germany 6.0M, Austria 1.25M, Czechia 1.44M, Switzerland 0.5M, Netherlands 0.5M, ~60% of Belgium 0.54M, Slovenia 0.2M, imperial northern and central Italy ~55% of Italy's 8.5M = 4.7M, plus the Kingdom of Arles/Burgundy and Lorraine in modern France ~1.5M = ~16.6M. Range covers uncertainty over how much of Italy obeyed the emperor in 1200.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Lombard and Tuscan cities (Milan ~ 60,000-100,000) raise the average; Germany proper ~3-5%.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element: the household knights and imperial ministeriales of the two rival kings, Philip of Swabia and Otto IV, plus castle garrisons on royal domain. Barbarossa's Italian army at Legnano (1176) was ~3,000 heavy cavalry (Grillo 2024, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Legnano). audit 2026-10-30: date basis: a year without a general muster, so only the household element is active and campaign levies are trainedReserves (france-1415, dated to the Agincourt campaign, counts its assembled army instead).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Knights and mounted sergeants owing imperial service (Heerfahrt) through princes and bishops; the 981 Indiculus loricatorum asked ~2,000 armoured horsemen of the German churches alone for one Italian campaign. Contingents arrive in weeks, not days.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Household officials, engineers, carters.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Knightly class plus communal militias of German and Italian towns.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Household knights and ministeriales in full mail on barded or unbarded destriers.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: mail hauberk, great helm emerging, couched lance; among the best in Europe.

count.note: Educated guess. Castle garrison spearmen and mercenary foot (Brabanters).
Educated guess. Traction and early counterweight trebuchets built for sieges (Crema 1159, Milan 1162).

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: two rival kings during the throne war (1198-1208); princes followed their own interests.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25: feudal host split by civil war.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: after Henry VI's death (1197) the empire's fortunes turned.

armor.note: Anchor 4 minus: full mail, early great helm, no plate yet.

ships.note: Anchor 3-4: Baltic cogs (Luebeck), Italian galleys of nominally imperial Genoa and Pisa; no imperial navy.

fortification.note: Anchor 4: stone castles (Pfalzen, Reichsburgen), walled cities.

logistics.note: Anchor 3-4: river transport on Rhine and Danube, requisition.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) UK 1252-1270 ~1,200-1,400, Spain 1280 = 1,381, UK 1000 = 1,151 (2011 int$). Germany lagged England; Lombardy led Europe. Mid ~1,050.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Mostly service in kind; both claimants spent heavily to buy princes.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Italian and Rhenish crafts, mining (Goslar silver).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. High-medieval clearance and expansion.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roman roads in the Rhineland and Italy, Alpine pass roads, few elsewhere.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Luebeck, Bremen, Hamburg, Genoa, Pisa, Cologne (river).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Baltic and Rhine shipping plus nominally imperial Genoa and Pisa.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.15-0.3 oxen and horses per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: dense castle network and walled cities; civil war limits population support.

notes: Snapshot = 1200, during the throne war between Philip of Swabia (Hohenstaufen) and Otto IV (Welf). The Kingdom of Sicily (Frederick II, a minor) is not counted. No modern total for the imperial army exists; the household-plus-ministeriales active force and the knightly reserve are educated guesses anchored on Legnano (~3,000 imperial heavy horse, Grillo 2024) and Bouvines 1214, where Otto IV fielded 1,300-1,500 knights and ~7,500 infantry, mostly Flemish and Low Country allies (Verbruggen 1997, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Bouvines). Population convention: imperial Germany, Bohemia, the Low Countries, Burgundy-Arles and imperial Italy.
